inputs.text: Medium waist-up photograph at eye level, 35mm lens. A fictional adult woman in her thirties with a light chestnut chin-length softly waved bob and a side part looks down at a small brass pocket compass she holds in both hands at chest height. She wears a mustard-yellow canvas field coat with flap chest pockets, metal buttons and shoulder tabs, and a chunky teal cable-knit scarf wrapped around her neck. The compass is a real magnetic compass: a polished round brass case with its hinged brass lid open, a clear glass cover, a cream dial printed with four large bold black letters, N at the top, E on the right, S at the bottom and W on the left, a thin black degree tick ring around the edge, and one straight two-ended needle, red north half pointing to N and silver south half. The dial is tilted toward the camera so all four letters and the red needle are clearly readable. She stands beside a weathered wooden potting bench inside a rain-soaked Victorian greenhouse with a dark green painted window grid, rain droplets running down the glass panes, and potted ferns.
